Description Pricing is one of the most consequential decisions Amazon makes, and the science behind it needs to be causally rigorous, not just predictive. The P2 Optimization Science team builds the machine learning (ML) systems that power Amazon's pricing decisions at scale: demand lift models, customer lifetime value (LTV) frameworks, and the experimentation infrastructure that validates whether pricing changes actually work. We're looking for a Research Scientist to own causal inference at the intersection of ML and pricing experimentation. Our team has identified a real gap: the methodological bridge between econometric analysis and production-scale ML pipelines needs a practitioner who lives in both worlds. You'll build conditional average treatment effect (CATE) estimation models, design analysis workflows for pricing experiments, and develop reusable causal ML infrastructure that the broader team — including non-ML scientists — can rely on. If you're a scientist who wants to tackle hard causal identification problems in a high-stakes production environment, and who finds satisfaction in making rigorous methods accessible to a broader team, this role is for you. Key job responsibilities - Design, train, evaluate, and deploy end-to-end causal ML pipelines for pricing use cases, including CATE estimation models and heterogeneous treatment effect frameworks. - Serve as the team's causal ML methodology expert — defining identification strategies, model selection criteria, evaluation standards, and the tradeoffs between econometric and ML approaches to causal estimation. - Contribute causal analysis methodology to pricing A/B test post-analysis and build reusable tooling that economists and other non-ML scientists can adopt without requiring deep ML expertise. - Assess emerging causal inference methods (e.g., synthetic difference-in-differences, generalized random forests, causal representation learning) for applicability to Amazon's pricing context, and author internal methodology proposals for adoption. - Partner with senior economists on identification strategy and causal assumptions, collaborate with software and data engineering partners on production deployment, and align with product managers on experiment design requirements. A day in the life Your work directly shapes the prices customers see on hundreds of millions of Amazon products. In a given week you might investigate an optimization anomaly in simulation and trace it to an unmodeled market dynamic, then design an offline evaluation framework to benchmark competing approaches before committing to online testing. You'll collaborate with senior economists on identification strategy for a pricing experiment, present a science proposal for incorporating a new competitiveness signal into an optimization system, or work with the experimentation platform team on randomization design. You'll also have opportunities to write up novel scientific findings for submission to venues such as KDD, NeurIPS, or the ACM Conference on Economics and Computation. About the team The P2 Optimization Science team sits at the center of Amazon's pricing decisions. We build the ML systems, causal inference pipelines, and experimentation infrastructure that determine how prices are set across Amazon's global catalog. Our team brings together research scientists, economists, and engineers who collaborate closely to turn rigorous methodology into production-quality systems with measurable business impact. We value scientific rigor, clear communication across disciplines, and a culture where every team member's work is designed to be extensible and useful beyond their own project. If you want your science to directly influence how hundreds of millions of customers experience Amazon, this is the team to join. Basic Qualifications - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of quantitative field research experience - Experience investigating the feasibility of applying scientific principles and concepts to business problems and products - Experience analyzing both experimental and observational data sets Preferred Qualifications - Knowledge of R, MATLAB, Python or similar scripting language - Experience with agile development - Experience building web based dashboards using common frameworks - In depth familiarity with the literature and practice of operations management, supply chain management, inventory management, revenue management, forecasting, and/or logistics - Prior well-established recognized academic experience, multiple publications in top-tier academic journals Programming experience using at least one modern programming language such as Python, Java, or C++ - Proficiency in model development, model validation and model implementation for large-scale applications - Experience with developing prototypes by manipulating and analyzing complex, high-volume, high-dimensionality data from varying sources Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. full_description:
Department Overview

The appointee shall provide services as assigned by the supervisor in furtherance of the university’s missions and goals of teaching, research, patient care, outreach and public service.

This position reports to (supervisor): Valerie King, Clinical Research Director

Function/Duties of Position

Independently Develop, Write, and Present Evidence Synthesis Research Products for Policymaker Audiences

  • Lead the preparation of research products for public payers and health policy decision makers according to Center research methods, and style guidelines, ensuring accuracy and clarity, and using narrative text, tables, and appropriate illustrations.
  • Serve as a clinical leader in the interpretation and communication of evidence, policy, and research findings to state policymakers and other decision makers through webinars, meetings, conferences and other forums.
  • Research and analyze the context of client question(s) and convert into structured, answerable research questions.
  • Work with an information specialist to construct and carry out appropriate search strategies addressing research questions posed by clients.
  • Identify relevant research studies, additional grey literature, clinical practice guidelines, and policy documents, and determine their relevance to the research question(s).
  • Critically evaluate the risk of bias and applicability of included research studies and clinical practice guidelines.
  • Appropriately assign a certainty of evidence rating (e.g., GRADE) from the body of evidence for select outcomes.
  • Conduct or collaborate with colleagues to perform meta-analyses for evidence synthesis projects, as needed.
  • Manage evidence synthesis steps and workflow using structured systematic review software (e.g., DistillerSR)
  • Develop interview protocols and conduct interviews with key informants, as needed.
  • Identify and contextualize relevant federal, state, and organizational policy documents and develop considerations that integrate evidence, policy context and other information relevant for policymakers.
  • Create and manage references in a citation management software program (e.g., EndNote).
  • Collaborate with data analysts and other team members on quantitative analyses and the interpretation of findings to support evidence-informed policy and program decision-making.
  • Provide clinical consultation and interpretation to interdisciplinary teams.

Provide Leadership for Potential and Ongoing Research Activities

  • Serve as a high-level project leader for technical assistance, health technology assessment programs, and other Center projects.
  • Serve as an initial reviewer of selected reports, and review research methods documents as directed by the Research Directors.
  • Contribute to development of research and report methodology.
  • Contribute to requests for proposal submissions for relevant projects.
  • Contribute to the ongoing Center development and various project deliverables via participation in selected project teams and staff meetings.
  • Provide training, mentorship, and supervision to Research Associates, Policy Analysts, and other colleagues at the Center, as needed.
  • Provide clinical consultation, subject matter expertise, and knowledge of Medicaid or other payer policy development to researchers, policy analysts, data analysts and other Center staff to support the design, interpretation and communication of research, analyses and technical assistance provided to Center clients.

Project Management

  • Track project progress, anticipate next steps, and coordinate with internal and external stakeholders to ensure the timely delivery of high-quality research products.
  • Manage assigned project activities, timelines, and deliverables, proactively identifying and addressing barriers to project completion.
  • Incorporate feedback constructively and efficiently, revising work products as needed to meet project objectives, methodological standards, and client needs.
  • Adapt work products as needed to meet project objectives, methodological standards and client needs.

Communication and Dissemination

  • Develop and maintain effective relationships with Center clients, research partners, data and policy resources, and a wide range of state and federal agencies, healthcare organizations and stakeholders.
  • Represent the Center effectively at selected national and state conferences, meetings, and other professional forums, preparing materials and delivering presentations that effectively communicate evidence, research findings, and policy considerations to diverse audiences, including senior policymakers and other decision makers.

Required Qualifications

  • MD, DO, PharmD, other clinical discipline (e.g., nursing, psychology) with relevant doctoral degree, or other relevant PhD or equivalent terminal degree; or equivalent combination of clinical expertise with additional experience and education in health policy. Extensive coursework in epidemiology, biostatistics, public health, and research methodology.

  • At least 10 years’ experience applying these skills to support health policy decision making.

  • Experience working with Medicaid or another government-administered health or human services program in a policy, research, analytic, clinical or administrative capacity.

  • Demonstrated ability to synthesize and interpret evidence and translate complex findings into clear, actionable written products and oral presentations for policymakers and other decision makers.

  • Experience presenting research findings and policy-relevant evidence, with a high degree of facility, to diverse audiences, including public sector leaders and decision makers.

  • Strong research skills, including expertise in study design, evidence synthesis, critical appraisal, epidemiology, biostatistics,quantitative and qualitative methods, and policy analysis.

  • Experience producing, evaluating and adapting systematic reviews and meta-analyses to support policy and program decision making.

  • Experience critically appraising research studies, systematic reviews, clinical practice guidelines, and related evidence sources.

  • Experience assessing the risk of bias and certainty of evidence (e.g., GRADE).

  • Demonstrated ability to provide clinical expertise and consultation to interdisciplinary teams, including researchers, policy analysts, data analysts and others to support the interpretation and application of evidence.

  • Experience working with or in government-administered health or human service programs, including policy development, administration, research or analysis, with demonstrated understanding of state health policy and Medicaid.

  • Experience in applying evidence and policy research to support public decision making processes.

  • Experience working collabotatively within interdisciplinary research environments to develop high quality products that meet client needs and timelines.

  • Strong project management skills, including the ability to lead research activities, mange multiple priorities, and deliver high quality products on time and within budget.

  • Ability to adapt and refine work processes and products in response to client needs, evolving policy environments and stakeholder feedback.

  • Excellent writing, editing and proofreading skills, including the ability to adhere to style guidelines and respond constructively to to reviewer and editor feedback.

  • Proficiency in Microsoft Office applications, including Word, PowerPoint, Excel, Outlook.

  • Experience using systematic review, citation management, and related research software applications (e.g., EndNote, DistillerSR).

  • Excellent organizational skills and ability to manage multiple projects and competing priorities simultaneously.

  • Excellent interpersonal, verbal and written communication skills.

  • Ability to develop productive relationships with clients, colleagues, policymakers, researchers and other stakeholders.

  • Ability to provide training, mentorship and guidance to colleagues and project teams, as needed.

  • Ability to interact productively with clients and engage them in projects.

  • Ability to exercise sound judgment and discretion, maintain confidentiality, professional demeanor and attitude in all situations, including sensitive or high-profile situations.

  • Ability to work independently while contributing effectively to team environments.

Preferred Qualifications

  • Master’s degree or PhD in epidemiology, biostatistics or statistics.

  • Experience working with systematic review software applications (e.g., DistillerSR).

  • Experience conducting meta-analysis using common software applications (e.g., RevMan, Stata).

  • Experience analyzing primary and secondary datasets, particularly state-level datasets from programs such as Medicaid.

  • Experience conducting cost-benefit-analysis, program evaluation, or economic analyses.

  • Record of peer-reviewed publications.

Additional Details

Ability to travel within state or out of state for meetings, if needed.

Why apply to OHSU?

We are Oregon's only public academic health center. In addition to caring for patients, we lead groundbreaking research. We also train the next generation of health care professionals. As Portland's largest employer, we give you opportunities to learn and advance in a system of hospitals and clinics across Oregon and Southwest Washington. All are welcome. OHSU welcomes people of all ages, ethnicities, genders, national origins, religions and sexual orientations. We are striving to build an anti-racist, multicultural institution and encourage people with diverse backgrounds to apply. To request reasonable accommodation, contact askhr@ohsu.edu

Description Great code assistants have to understand code the way an experienced engineer does, not as a wall of text but as a living structure of symbols, calls, types, and dependencies that span an entire repository. Most AI tools today flatten all of that into tokens and lose the structure that makes real software navigable. Amazon Web Services (AWS) is assembling an elite team of scientists and engineers to fix that, and we are hiring an Applied Scientist to build the intelligence layer that lets our AI development tools reason about code through its true structure. You will help create generative AI technologies, including Kiro IDE and CLI, that are transforming how software gets built. You will design how we turn the many signals around code, from static analysis and symbol graphs to build systems and language servers, into a single unified representation our models can reason over. This is a build-oriented research role where the questions are still open: how to fuse heterogeneous code signals, how to represent a whole repository so a model can find and use the right context, and how to ground an assistant's reasoning in the structure of real software rather than text alone. Your work will reach millions of developers, and you will own this direction end to end, from framing the approach to shipping it in a product engineers rely on every day. Key job responsibilities - Design a unified representation of code that fuses static analysis, symbol and call graphs, type information, and build system context - Build the methods and models that consume that representation to power code navigation, retrieval, and reasoning at repository scale - Invent and implement state-of-the-art machine learning solutions that operate at unprecedented Amazon scale - Deploy products that directly impact the daily workflows of millions of developers worldwide - Publish and present your work at premier ML, NLP, and software engineering conferences (NeurIPS, ICML, ICLR, ACL, EMNLP, ICSE, FSE) - Accelerate innovation by working directly with customers to rapidly transition research breakthroughs into production systems About the team Why AWS? Amazon Web Services (AWS) is the world’s most comprehensive and broadly adopted cloud platform. We pioneered cloud computing and never stopped innovating — that’s why customers from the most successful startups to Global 500 companies trust our robust suite of products and services to power their businesses. Inclusive Team Culture Here at AWS, it’s in our nature to learn and be curious. Our employee-led affinity groups foster a culture of inclusion that empower us to be proud of our differences. Ongoing events and learning experiences, including our Conversations on Race and Ethnicity (CORE) and AmazeCon conferences, inspire us to never stop embracing our uniqueness. Mentorship & Career Growth We’re continuously raising our performance bar as we strive to become Earth’s Best Employer. That’s why you’ll find endless knowledge-sharing, mentorship and other career-advancing resources here to help you develop into a better-rounded professional. Work/Life Balance We value work-life harmony. Achieving success at work should never come at the expense of sacrifices at home, which is why we strive for flexibility as part of our working culture. When we feel supported in the workplace and at home, there’s nothing we can’t achieve in the cloud. Hybrid Work We value innovation and recognize this sometimes requires uninterrupted time to focus on a build. We also value in-person collaboration and time spent face-to-face. Our team affords employees options to work in the office every day or in a flexible, hybrid work model near one of our U.S. Amazon offices. Basic Qualifications - 3+ years of building models for business application experience - PhD, or Master's degree and 4+ years of CS, CE, ML or related field experience - Experience in patents or publications at top-tier peer-reviewed conferences or journals - Experience programming in Java, C++, Python or related language - Experience in any of the following areas: algorithms and data structures, parsing, numerical optimization, data mining, parallel and distributed computing, high-performance computing Preferred Qualifications - Experience using Unix/Linux - Experience in professional software development Amazon is an equal opportunity employer and does not discriminate on the basis of protected veteran status, disability, or other legally protected status. Description Prime Video is a first-stop entertainment destination offering customers a vast collection of premium programming in one app available across thousands of devices. Prime members can customize their viewing experience and find their favorite movies, series, documentaries, and live sports – including Amazon MGM Studios-produced series and movies; licensed fan favorites; and programming from Prime Video subscriptions such as Apple TV+, HBO Max, Peacock, Crunchyroll and MGM+. All customers, regardless of whether they have a Prime membership or not, can rent or buy titles via the Prime Video Store, and can enjoy even more content for free with ads. Are you interested in shaping the future of entertainment? Prime Video's technology teams are creating best-in-class digital video experience. As a Prime Video team member, you’ll have end-to-end ownership of the product, user experience, design, and technology required to deliver state-of-the-art experiences for our customers. You’ll get to work on projects that are fast-paced, challenging, and varied. You’ll also be able to experiment with new possibilities, take risks, and collaborate with remarkable people. We’ll look for you to bring your diverse perspectives, ideas, and skill-sets to make Prime Video even better for our customers. With global opportunities for talented technologists, you can decide where a career Prime Video Tech takes you! Key job responsibilities The science challenges include: - Heterogeneous customer responses. The same customer responds differently to ads depending on what they’re watching, how engaged they are, and their broader streaming context. We need to understand and predict this variation to make better advertising decisions in real time. - Signal sparsity in streaming. Unlike search or retail advertising, streaming offers no clicks, no conversions, and limited direct feedback. We must develop creative approaches to infer customer preferences, intent, and tolerance from indirect behavioral signals. - Personalization at scale. A one-size-fits-all ad experience leaves value on the table for both customers and the business. We build systems that adapt ad load, placement, and content to individual viewers across 100M+ customers and 100k+ titles. - Small effects, large variance. Ad interventions typically produce 0.1-2% shifts in engagement, effects easily overwhelmed by natural behavioral variance. Measuring, attributing, and optimizing these small signals requires rigorous experimental design and causal methodologies. - Competing objectives. Revenue, customer engagement, long-term retention, and advertiser value are in tension. We develop principled frameworks to navigate these tradeoffs and optimize for sustainable outcomes rather than any single metric. A day in the life - Contribute to the research and development of ML models that personalize advertising decisions for 100M+ customers across 100k+ titles, with production deployment in mind - Develop deep learning architectures (multi-task learning, embedding-based representations) for customer behavior prediction at scale - Design and analyze large-scale A/B experiments, applying causal inference techniques to measure and optimize the impact of ad strategies on customer engagement and monetization - Partner with engineering to ensure models meet production latency and scalability requirements - Collaborate with product managers to frame business problems as tractable ML problems and translate findings into product decisions - Shape the team’s scientific roadmap, identifying high-impact research directions About the team Prime Video Ads is pioneering the use of Generative AI, Deep Learning and Causal ML to empower the next generation of Ads experience in Prime Video. Our vision is to build the world’s most valuable and differentiated ad-supported streaming platform: one where every ad is relevant to the viewer, and every dollar spent by an advertiser delivers measurable results. We are seeking lead applied scientists who have demonstrated experience in advancing state of the art ML algorithms, particularly in Personalization, Relevance, Casual Inference and Gen-AI areas.
